title: Departed Officer's Modification Approval Against Updated Delegation Matrix
scenario_text:
**FIS Horizon — Loan Modification Record (Loan #CL-2023-06290)**
Borrower: Meridian Logistics Group LLC | Original Commitment: $6.0M term loan | Current Outstanding: $4.1M
Modification Date: 06/15/2025 | Type: Covenant waiver + amortization extension
Modification Details: Waived DSCR covenant (1.20x minimum) for Q2/Q3 2025; extended amortization from 20yr to 25yr; reduced quarterly principal from $75K to $60K.
Approving Officer: R. Hargrove, SVP Commercial Lending
Risk Rating: 6 (Special Mention)

**Workday — HR Record**
Robert Hargrove | Title at termination: SVP, Commercial Lending | Termination date: 08/30/2025 | Reason: Voluntary resignation
Delegation of Authority (at time of departure): Up to $5.0M for standard modifications; up to $3.0M for classified asset modifications (Risk Rating 6+)

**SharePoint — Delegation of Authority Matrix (Version 3.2, effective 03/01/2025)**
SVP, Commercial Lending:
- Standard modifications (Risk Rating 1-5): Up to $5.0M
- Classified asset modifications (Risk Rating 6-8): Up to $3.0M
- Modifications involving covenant waivers on classified assets: Up to $2.0M (requires co-approval from Credit Risk Officer)
[Version 2.8 (effective 01/2024) stated: 'SVP authority for all modification types: Up to $5.0M']

**Microsoft Teams — #credit-risk (06/10/2025, 2:15 PM)**
@r.hargrove: Running a mod through on Meridian Logistics — covenant waiver plus amor extension. Total exposure $4.1M, rated 6. Need anything from your side?
@k.patel (Credit Risk Officer): What's the total mod value? Is this just the waiver or are we looking at economic impact of the amor change?
@r.hargrove: Waiver is temporary (2 quarters). Amor extension reduces payment by $15K/qtr. Total economic concession maybe $200K NPV?
@k.patel: Should be fine. 👍
[No further messages in thread]

**Outlook — Email (09/15/2025)**
From: audit-findings@cascadefinancial.com
To: t.whitfield@cascadefinancial.com; chief.credit.officer@cascadefinancial.com
Subject: Loan Modification Audit — Q2/Q3 2025 Sample

'During our sample review of loan modifications, we identified Loan #CL-2023-06290 (Meridian Logistics) as potentially exceeding the approving officer's delegated authority. Under DOA Matrix v3.2 (effective 03/2025), covenant waivers on classified assets require Credit Risk Officer co-approval with a $2.0M cap. The modification was on a $4.1M classified asset. Please confirm proper authorization was obtained.'

**ServiceNow — Audit Response Tracking (AR-2025-0087)**
Status: Open | Due: 10/15/2025 | Assigned: T. Whitfield
Comment (09/18/2025, @t.whitfield): 'Reviewing. Hargrove departed 08/30. Need to determine if Teams exchange with Patel constitutes co-approval.'
Comment (09/22/2025, @compliance.review): 'DOA Matrix requires co-approval to be documented in the credit file. A Teams thumbs-up does not meet documentation standards per Policy 12.1(b). However, if Patel confirms intent, a retroactive memo may cure the deficiency.'
question: Regarding the audit finding on the Meridian Logistics modification: was the modification validly approved, and what remediation (if any) is required?

contributor.name: Thomas Whitfield
contributor.title: VP, Commercial Lending
contributor.domain_expertise: Loan origination, credit policy, covenant compliance, loan modifications, workout situations

choices: The modification was validly approved — Hargrove had $5.0M authority for all modification types under the DOA Matrix that was current when the loan was originally booked (v2.8)
The modification was validly approved — Patel's thumbs-up in Teams constitutes co-approval from the Credit Risk Officer, satisfying the DOA Matrix v3.2 two-signature requirement
The modification is void and must be unwound — Hargrove acted outside his authority on a classified asset, making the covenant waiver and amortization extension unenforceable

The modification exceeded Hargrove's authority and the Teams thumbs-up from Patel does not constitute valid co-approval; the modification must be re-ratified by an officer with proper authority and a retroactive credit memo must be filed
